**A Heartbreaking Review: A Salon Experience That Left Me Feeling Betrayed**

As an African American woman, I’ve always taken pride in finding salons that understand and cater to my unique hair needs. I wanted to share my experience at a local salon that initially seemed like a safe haven, but what followed was a nightmare that left me questioning whether I could ever trust another stylist again.

At first, the salon was everything I’d hoped for. The stylist took the time to understand my hair type and suggested treatments that left my curls looking vibrant and healthy. For the first few weeks, I felt like I’d found my sanctuary. My hair was receiving compliments non-stop, and I walked with newfound confidence.

But then, things took a tragic turn. After about a month, I noticed my hair was breaking off in my hands. Each brush stroke left my strands snaps, and the once-lush curls became a sad memory. I was horrified, thinking I was doing everything right—using the products they recommended, following their advice to a tee. I returned, hoping for answers, but the owner didn’t seem fazed. Instead of offering solutions, she dismissed my concerns with a shrug and told me it was just part of having curly hair.

This wasn’t just about hair; it was about trust. I felt like I’d been misled, like I was walking an invisible tightrope, trying to maintain my dignity while my confidence unraveled alongside my hair. Every time I looked in the mirror, I saw the damage, and it hurt. It wasn’t just about my appearance; it was about the self-esteem I’d worked so hard to build.

Desperate for a solution, I forked out for an expensive treatment they advertised as a miracle cure. It was a gamble, and it failed miserably. My hair became worse—dry, brittle, and breaking more than ever. The owner didn’t even have the decency to apologize. Instead, she blamed my lack of care, acting as though I was to blame for the mess my hair was in.

This experience has left me scarred. I can’t help but wonder how many others have been through the same. To anyone reading this, I beg you: trust your instincts. Don’t be lured in by empty promises and a facade. Your hair is your crown; don’t let anyone take that from you. This salon preyed on my community’s desire to feel beautiful and then left us feeling broken. We deserve better. Run, don’t walk, away from this place. Your hair—and your self-respect—are worth it.<｜end▁of▁sentence｜>
